package_info.why_malicious: The package contains embedded credential-stealing malware that executes a password recovery tool, collects browser-stored credentials, and exfiltrates them to an external server. The code is intentionally obfuscated within a legitimate-seeming package, deletes evidence after exfiltration, and is not expected in any legitimate npm package.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the package is executed as part of a build or script)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file of bb-builder package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes a bundled password recovery tool (WebBrowserPassView) to extract browser-stored credentials, saves the output to an HTML file, reads the file, sends its contents via HTTP POST to a remote server, and deletes the file to remove evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes an external credential recovery tool, collects sensitive data, exfiltrates it to an external server, and deletes evidence. This is classic credential-stealing malware behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal npm package should not execute external binaries, harvest credentials, or communicate with unknown external servers. Legitimate packages do not perform credential theft or anti-forensics.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password recovery tools may be used locally by users for legitimate recovery, but never as part of an npm package or with automatic exfiltration.
key_indicators: Automated reading and exfiltration of credential data
Use of HTTP POST to unknown external server

attack_chain.action: User installs or executes the bb-builder package, triggering the malicious JavaScript code.
The package executes WebBrowserPassView to extract browser-stored credentials and saves them to an HTML file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential data is available on disk

attack_chain.action: The package reads the credential data from the HTML file and sends it via HTTP POST to the attacker's server.
The package deletes the HTML file containing the credentials to remove evidence.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of external credential recovery tools (e.g., WebBrowserPassView) from within npm packages
Automated reading and exfiltration of credential data files
Immediate deletion of files after exfiltration (anti-forensics)
Unexpected HTTP POST requests to unknown domains during package execution
file_indicators: Presence of WebBrowserPassView or similar binaries in npm package directories
Creation and deletion of files named out.html or similar in working directories
Suspicious executable files bundled within JavaScript packages
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to 1.host.jwte.ch:1337/pwn or similar credential collection endpoints
Outbound network connections from build or install scripts to unknown domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that bundle and execute credential recovery tools, especially those that create temporary files containing credentials and immediately delete them. Flag any package that makes HTTP POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains during installation or runtime. Use static analysis to detect embedded binaries and dynamic analysis to observe file and network behaviors during package execution.
